QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_86

question.text: A portfolio worth Rs. 6 crore has a beta of 1.3. The fund manager wants to INCREASE the portfolio beta to 1.8 using Nifty futures (at 25,000, lot size 65). Using the standard hedge-ratio formula applied to the beta gap, how many contracts should be BOUGHT?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the standard index-futures hedge-ratio formula to the beta gap: 1. Beta gap = Target beta - Current beta = 1.8 - 1.3 = 0.5 2. Portfolio value = Rs. 6,00,00,000 3. Futures contract value = 25,000 x 65 = Rs. 16,25,000 4. Contracts to BUY = (6,00,00,000 x 0.5) / 16,25,000 = 3,00,00,000 / 16,25,000 ≈ 18.46 ≈ 18 contracts To increase market exposure (raise beta), long futures are bought; to reduce exposure (lower beta), futures are sold. The Trap: Selling futures decreases beta, so "18 SOLD" gets the direction wrong. 48 contracts uses 1.3 as the multiplier instead of the gap; 67 uses 1.8 instead of the gap. Only the difference (0.5) belongs in the formula. Note: Pages 52-54 and 92-93 of the Series VIII workbook support portfolio beta, contract value, the hedge-ratio formula for hedging portfolio risk, and the direction of long versus short futures. The exact "target beta minus current beta" rule is an inference from the hedge-ratio formula rather than a verbatim quote in the pages checked.
